claim: Claude Code PreToolUse hook can modify input (updatedInput field), PostToolUse can modify output (updatedToolOutput), both can block via decision=block
evidence: Primary source (the claim's own cited page), verbatim from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks — "PreToolUse decision control" section: PreToolUse table lists ONLY `permissionDecision` ("allow"/"deny"/"ask"/"defer"), `permissionDecisionReason`, `updatedInput` ("Object with fields that replace the tool's input arguments before it runs"), and `additionalContext` — there is NO top-level `decision` field; blocking is done via `permissionDecision: "deny"`. Confirmed by full-page search: the word "approve" does not appear anywhere, and no legacy top-level `decision` field is documented for PreToolUse. "PostToolUse decision control" section: uses top-level `{"decision":"block","reason":...}` to block, and `updatedToolOutput` ("String that replaces the tool's output before it reaches Claude"). So updatedInput (PreToolUse) and updatedToolOutput (PostToolUse) are both correct, but the "both can block via decision=block" clause is false: PreToolUse blocks via hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision:"deny", not decision:"block". (In-repo lib/validate-at-stop.sh uses {"decision":"block"} but that is the Stop hook, a different post-execution event, not PreToolUse.)
correction: PreToolUse can modify tool input via `hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput`, and blocks/denies a tool via `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: "deny"` (values allow/deny/ask/defer) — it has NO top-level `decision` field. PostToolUse can replace tool output via `hookSpecificOutput.updatedToolOutput` and blocks via top-level `{"decision": "block", "reason": ...}`. Only PostToolUse uses `decision: "block"`; PreToolUse does not.

The cited manual artifact (dev/scripts/kiro-memory-hitl.sh) is a plain env-gated dev script (MEM_SCRATCH/PROJ overrides), not a flake app or devenv task, and it exists for closed-binary verification, not because the hooks invoke an agent or require authentication. claim: Both Claude Code and Kiro CLI fail to fire hooks for a subagent's own tool calls — Kiro #7755 (docs say 'Hooks will not trigger in subagents') and Claude #34692 (closed 'not planned', affected 2.1.76+).

Issue #34692 is a single community bug report (author_association NONE) against v2.1.76 that was auto-closed as stale by github-actions[bot], not a maintainer "not planned" WONTFIX, and its "affected 2.1.76+ / persists" implication is contradicted by the current docs. A defensible restatement: "Kiro CLI documents that hooks do not trigger in subagents (open feature request #7755); a single Claude Code bug report (#34692, v2.1.76, stale-closed by a bot) alleged the same, but current Claude Code docs indicate PreToolUse/PostToolUse do fire inside subagents (dedicated agent_id/agent_type fields)."
evidence: Claude hooks docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks): agent_id "Present only when the hook fires inside a subagent call. Use this to distinguish subagent hook calls from main-thread calls"; agent_type "Present when the session uses --agent or the hook fires inside a subagent"; nested agentic loop lists "PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, SubagentStart/Stop, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted". GitHub API for anthropics/claude-code#34692: title matches, body cites version 2.1.76, state=closed, state_reason=not_planned, closed_by=github-actions[bot] (stale auto-close, closed_at 2026-05-30), author_association=NONE, labels [bug, has repro, area:hooks, area:agents]. Kiro docs (kiro.dev/docs/chat/subagents/) verbatim: "Steering files and MCP servers work in subagents exactly as they do in the main agent. However, subagents do not have access to Specs, and Hooks will not trigger in subagents." GitHub API for kirodotdev/Kiro#7755: title "Hooks should trigger in subagents - governance must be uniform across all agent types", state=open, labels [cli], body quotes the Kiro docs sentence. Residual nuance: the Claude docs do not contain one single sentence explicitly stating "PreToolUse fires for subagent tool calls," but the documented per-call agent_id/agent_type fields plus the nested-loop event list weigh strongly against the blanket "fails to fire".

claim: Claude MCP env field replaces the process env, stripping PATH, so hook/MCP wrappers must use absolute store paths or bare commands fail silently; the repo already enforces this via checks/bare-commands.nix and getExe/runtimeInputs.
evidence: Authoritative MCP TypeScript SDK, packages/client/src/client/stdio.ts (modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk, main @ f413763): StdioClientTransport.start() spawns with `env: { ...getDefaultEnvironment(), ...this._serverParams.env }` (comment: "merge default env with server env because mcp server needs some env vars"), and `DEFAULT_INHERITED_ENV_VARS` on POSIX = ['HOME','LOGNAME','PATH','SHELL','TERM','USER']. PATH is explicitly in the default-inherited set and is merged in even when a custom `env` is supplied — so setting `env` does NOT strip PATH; the child gets a curated SUBSET of the parent env, not an empty/replaced env. Official Claude Code MCP docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) are silent on replace-vs-merge and imply a constructed server env (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR "set in the server's environment"; plugin servers get "the same environment variables as manually configured servers"). The widely-documented real failure (emmanuelbernard.com 2025-04-07; anthropics/claude-code#1254, closed not-planned) is a minimal/curated inherited-environment problem, not env-replacement-stripping-PATH. In-repo enforcement DOES exist and is correctly described: checks/bare-commands.nix (lines 4-7 assert the mechanism; wired as bareCommandsCheck in flake.nix:204) lints bare coreutils in lib/ + packages/*/lib/; lib/mcp.nix:117-149 uses ${pkgs.coreutils}/bin/cat and getExe in mkSecretsWrapper; source fragment dev/fragments/nix-standards/nix-standards.md:29-35. But the fragment's and check's stated rationale ("env REPLACES the process environment entirely ... no PATH") contradicts the SDK. Repo's own memory (project_mcp_startup_failures.md) even attributes a related failure to "bare python3/jq not being on NixOS PATH" — the curated-PATH-lacking-store-paths mechanism, not PATH-stripping.
correction: The in-repo half is true (checks/bare-commands.nix + getExe/${pkgs.coreutils} enforce absolute paths), but the causal mechanism is wrong. Claude Code's stdio MCP servers inherit only a CURATED SUBSET of the parent environment — via the MCP SDK, getDefaultEnvironment() (HOME, LOGNAME, PATH, SHELL, TERM, USER on POSIX) MERGED with the server's `env` map. PATH is in that inherited set and is NOT stripped by setting `env`; it is lost only if you explicitly set PATH empty, or (on NixOS) the inherited PATH simply lacks the /nix/store bin paths a wrapper needs. So absolute store paths in wrappers are correct DEFENSIVE practice, but the accurate reason is "MCP children get a curated env subset and cannot rely on an enriched/NixOS PATH," not "the env field replaces the process env and strips PATH." (Note: pre-merge SDK versions did set env≈params.env, so the 'strips PATH' framing may have been accurate when root-caused in ~2025-2026, but is not accurate for the current SDK; residual uncertainty remains because Claude Code is closed-source and its exact bundled spawn cannot be read directly. Also, hooks — unlike MCP servers — run via the user's shell and inherit the full environment, so lumping "hook wrappers" into the same mechanism is imprecise.)

claim: Nix does not need to concatenate scripts for Claude — emit each contributor as a separate array entry and the CLI unions/aggregates them.

claim: devenv route `claude.code.hooks = (cfg.settings.hooks or {}) // cfg.hooks` conflates event-wiring JSON with script-body lines into one option — a right-biased override that would clobber (not union) a shared event key; latent schema mismatch vs HM's two-surface split.
evidence: mkClaude.nix:507 (devenv projection, inside `{ claude.code = { … hooks = …; }; }` at lines 501-509): `hooks = (cfg.settings.hooks or {}) // cfg.hooks;` — verbatim. Upstream HM module (…/programs/claude-code/options.nix:266-267) `hooks = attrsOf lines` written as hook script FILES (default.nix:281 mkHookEntries), while `settings` (options.nix:77-78, example :99-110) is freeform JSON whose `hooks` key is event-wiring `{PreToolUse=[{matcher;hooks=[{type;command}]}]}` written to settings.json (default.nix:236) — two distinct shapes on two surfaces. Decisive (claim's unverified part): devenv `claude.code.hooks` (…/devenv-source/src/modules/integrations/claude.nix:237-241) is a submodule `freeformType = attrsOf hookSubmodule`, hookSubmodule (:35-99) = {enable,name,hookType(enum),matcher,command(required)} — a structured record matching NEITHER script-body strings NOR event→list. `//` is right-biased shallow (would clobber, not deep-merge, on any key collision). correction: Core claim holds, with two refinements. claim: Generated hook scripts must be baked with writeShellScript (strict-mode header) and referenced by ABSOLUTE store path in command, because Claude/Kiro hook+MCP env REPLACES process env (bare names lose PATH). autoMemory.nix already does exactly this.
evidence: Official Claude Code hooks docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) directly contradict the hook-env-replacement rationale: "A hook process inherits the parent environment, so it can read $ANTHROPIC_MODEL if you set it in your shell" and "Handlers run in the current directory with Claude Code's environment." Hooks inherit PATH; they do not have env replaced. The cited claude-rules-nix-standards.md ("Shell Wrappers: Absolute Paths Required") scopes the replacement precisely and ONLY to the MCP config: "Claude Code's MCP `env` field replaces the process environment entirely" (root-caused via github-mcp/kagi-mcp) — it never claims hooks lose PATH. The repo's own code corroborates hook PATH inheritance: packages/kiro-cli/lib/autoMemory.nix:130 does `export PATH=${omBinPath}:"$PATH"` (prepends to an inherited $PATH), and overlays/kiro-memory-distiller.nix:16-18 puts git on PATH "ambient-first," deliberately preferring the inherited PATH's git — both meaningless if the env were replaced. The v3 hook action schema has no env field at all (mkKiro.nix:294: action:{type, command|prompt}), so there is no hook-env replacement mechanism. The other two sub-parts ARE true: autoMemory.nix:127-136 bakes writeShellScript wrappers with the strict-mode header (set -euETo pipefail / inherit_errexit) referenced by absolute store path in each command (lines 179/185/191/197), and MCP env replacement is genuine — but the claim's load-bearing "because … hook … env REPLACES process env (bare names lose PATH)" is false for hooks.
correction: autoMemory.nix does bake writeShellScript strict-mode hook wrappers referenced by absolute store path (CONFIRMED), and absolute store paths in generated shell wrappers are the correct repo convention. But the env-REPLACEMENT rationale applies specifically to the MCP server `env` config field, NOT to hooks: per official Claude Code docs, hook processes INHERIT the parent environment (PATH included), and autoMemory.nix itself relies on that inherited $PATH (prepends omBinPath to "$PATH"; git resolves ambient-first). Hooks have no `env` field to replace anything (v3 schema: action:{type, command|prompt}). The real reasons to use store paths in hook wrappers are (a) it is the natural Nix build output plus defensive convention, and (b) v3 hooks must be real workspace-local files because it skips store symlinks — a separate constraint — not "hook env replaces process env / bare names lose PATH."

claim: Claude keys hooks BY EVENT (event→[matcher-group→handler-array]); Kiro keys BY NAMED RECORD (name→{trigger,matcher,action}). Typed shapes must key differently to match their file formats; the only shared substructure is {event/trigger,matcher?,command}.

(1) Claude settings.json IS event-keyed: code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks shows `hooks -> {PreToolUse} -> [ {matcher, hooks:[{type,command}]} ]`. (2) Kiro v3 is NOT a name-keyed record: mkKiro.nix:292-298 (the claim's own cited source) documents `{version:"v1", hooks:[{name, description?, trigger, matcher?, action:{type,command|prompt}, timeout?, enabled?}]}` — a versioned ARRAY envelope; the official kiro.dev/docs/cli/v3/hooks states verbatim it is "a top-level version field paired with a hooks array—not a record keyed by hook name." `name`/`trigger`/`matcher`/`action` are fields inside each array element, and `command` is nested inside `action`, not a flat `{trigger,matcher,action}`. (3) Neither surface is a "typed shape": mkClaude.nix:250-251 `ai.claude.hooks = attrsOf lib.types.lines` (name→shell-script body); mkKiro.nix:316-320 `ai.kiro.hooks = attrsOf (either lines path)` marked "UNTYPED PASSTHROUGH" (mkKiro.nix:275-281); Claude `settings` is `freeformType = json` (mkClaude.nix:51-53). BOTH option surfaces key the same way (by name via attrsOf), so they do NOT "key differently."
correction: Claude Code hooks in settings.json ARE keyed by event (event → array of {matcher, hooks:[{type, command, ...}]}). But Kiro v3 hooks are NOT a name-keyed record: each .kiro/hooks/<name>.json is a versioned envelope {version:"v1", hooks:[{name, description?, trigger, matcher?, action:{type, command|prompt}, timeout?, enabled?}]} — a versioned ARRAY where name is a field, not the key, and command is nested inside action. In this repo neither hooks surface is a typed shape at all: ai.claude.hooks is attrsOf lines (name→script body), ai.kiro.hooks is attrsOf (either lines path) untyped passthrough, and Claude settings is freeform JSON. Both nix option surfaces are keyed identically (by name/attrsOf); the real difference is the file CONTENT each name maps to (a shell script for Claude vs a JSON hook-envelope for Kiro), not the keying.

claim: `nix flake check` builds sandboxed, pure derivations with no network/auth/credentials, so a real token-using live hook-fire test cannot run inside it at all — live firing MUST be a manual harness outside checks.
evidence: Nix manual (conf-file, `sandbox` option): value `relaxed` means "fixed-output derivations and derivations that have the `__noChroot` attribute set to `true` do not run in sandboxes" — such a check derivation gets full network + filesystem access. Nix glossary (fixed-output derivation): "the builder executable has access to the network" even under `sandbox = true` (FODs are not placed in a private network namespace). `sandbox = false` disables sandboxing entirely (default on macOS). On this host `nix config show sandbox` = true, confirming the DEFAULT premise. Repo's own docs/plans/prek-stop-hook-validator.md frames the stub-tool design as a deliberate choice ("deterministic and hermetic (no real linters in the sandbox)"), and checks/validate-at-stop.nix:8-17 stubs prek + uses a throwaway HOME — i.e. hermeticity was chosen, not forced.
correction: By DEFAULT (`sandbox = true`), a `nix flake check` derivation is sandboxed and pure — no network, no injected credentials — so the repo correctly runs its Stop-hook check against stub tools with a throwaway HOME, and a live token-using smoke test is best kept as a separate manual/CI harness. But this is a well-founded best-practice default, NOT a hard technical impossibility: Nix documents escape hatches — a `__noChroot = true` check with `sandbox = relaxed`, a fixed-output derivation (network-enabled even under strict sandbox), or `sandbox = false` — by which a networked, token-using test CAN be wired into a `nix flake check` build (token supplied impurely via `--impure`/`builtins.getEnv` or a readable path). So drop the categorical "cannot at all / MUST": prefer "by default should live outside checks."

claim: The natural composition mechanism [for hooks] is Nix listOf concatenation (module-system auto-concats listOf definitions), making the Nix merge isomorphic to the CLI runtime union; hooks must NOT use the collision-as-error mergeWithCollisionCheck used by the six keyed pools.
evidence: The authoritative hooks option is attrsOf lines, NOT listOf, in every source: repo ai.claude.hooks = `attrsOf lib.types.lines` (packages/claude-code/lib/mkClaude.nix:250-251, desc "Attribute name becomes the hook filename; value is the script body"); upstream home-manager programs.claude-code.hooks = `attrsOf lib.types.lines` (/nix/store/2c23lkh7...-source/modules/programs/claude-code/options.nix:266-267, written to ~/.claude/hooks/<name> via mkHookEntries, default.nix:281); ai.kiro.hooks = `attrsOf (either lines path)` (packages/kiro-cli/lib/mkKiro.nix:316-319). There is no listOf anywhere in the hooks data model. The six pools using mergeWithCollisionCheck (mcpServers, skills, rules, lspServers, environmentVariables, agents — lib/ai/app/hmTransform.nix:37-49; ai-common.nix:315-336) are ALL attrsOf; hooks are the SAME attrsOf/keyed-pool family, not a listOf. Primary docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) confirm a runtime union exists but over a three-level structure `{event: [{matcher, hooks:[...]}]}` with automatic dedup ("identical handlers are deduplicated automatically... by command string and args... HTTP hooks by URL") — a flat Nix listOf concat is a de-dup-free superset, not an isomorphism. The repo's own devenv hooks merge is `//` override, not list concat: `hooks = (cfg.settings.hooks or {}) // cfg.hooks` (mkClaude.nix:507).
correction: Hooks as actually modeled (both upstream programs.claude-code.hooks and this repo's ai.claude.hooks are `attrsOf lib.types.lines` — hook-script files keyed by filename) compose via attrsOf key-union with a per-key `lines` merge. That is a keyed pool structurally identical to the six mergeWithCollisionCheck pools, NOT listOf concatenation; no listOf exists in the hooks model, so "the natural composition mechanism is Nix listOf concatenation" is false. Claude Code's runtime does union hooks additively (this premise is correct), but over an attrsOf(event)→listOf(matcher) structure with automatic deduplication of identical handlers, so a plain Nix listOf concat is not isomorphic to it (Nix concat does not dedup and the structure is event-keyed, not flat). The normative conclusion is model-dependent, not universal: for the actual attrsOf-lines script-file model, two sources sharing a hook filename silently concatenate two script bodies into one corrupt file — exactly the footgun mergeWithCollisionCheck was built to catch — so collision-as-error is the consistent choice there, not something hooks "must NOT" use. Concatenation-not-collision would only be correct if hooks were modeled as the settings.json event→matcher arrays (settings.hooks) via the JSON freeform, which is a different option than the ai.claude.hooks pool the claim places alongside the six.
